messages.subject: Fill geom_text2 with background color
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

Please tell me if it is possible adding background color to geom_text2. It will cover the bottom layer and will make the labels clear. Below is an example.

tree <- rtree(25) ggtree(tree) + geom_text2(aes(label="D", subset=node==35))

I need the label "D" to be drawn on a white place.

Thank you!
Hovhannes

messages.subject: Stacked labels in facet bar plot with ggtree
messages.subject_clean: Stacked labels in facet bar plot with ggtree
messages.body_plain:
Hi!

I'm trying to figure out how to stack the labels in a faceted plot with ggtree. Currently, I have the tree and its respective stacked bar plot as shown in the first figure. However, the labels are neither centered nor correspond with the colored bar they should be.

Normally, in a stacked barplot using the geom_barh, it can be addressed by adding a position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5) to the geom_text element, but in this case, it is not working and is generating a weird result as shown in the second figure.

This is the code I'm using for adding the text labels to the Areas facet:

p2 <- facet_plot(p2, panel = "Areas", data = propByArea,
                 geom = geom_text,
                 mapping = aes(x = Proportion, label = Region.COD),
                 position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5))

Any idea of how to solve it?

messages.subject: Gheatmap with tree in fan layout with open angle
messages.subject_clean: Gheatmap with tree in fan layout with open angle
messages.body_plain:
Dear Yu,

First let me thank for your fantastic work on this package.
I never had to ask question in this conversation since the documentation is top notch and I always managed to find a way to do whatever I needed with ggtree.
Recently, though, I hit my first wall.

The issue is shortly described here (not by me, but this is the only ref I found about this specific issue/bug):

https://stackoverflow.com/questions/74076494/gheatmap-seems-to-close-open-angle-for-ggtree

The idea is that, to accommodate the variable names on the heatmap on a circular tree, I would like to use a fan representation with an open angle (30 or 45°) so that the names can lie vertically on the space that is not used by the phylogeny.
But, for now, calling gheatmap on a fan tree with an open angle seems to collapse the angle, for a reason you may able to investigate and maybe sort out.
There's no reason to put that on top of a priority list, but this feature could be useful especially for large matrix.
It would allow us to make similar representation as, e.g. this one from Anvi'o:

I think you get the idea.
Let me know if you feel interested, I can probably cook up a reproductible example with a toy dataset but I am not sure we need it at this point.
Best regards,

Etienne Loire
